The 2016–17 season of the [[Belgian First Division A]] was the 114th season of top-tier football in [[Belgium]] and the first following the structural changes in the Belgian football pyramid, reducing the number of professional teams to 24.{{cn|date=May 2016}} It began on 29 July 2016 and finished on 31 May 2017. The fixtures were announced on 8 June 2016.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sport.be/nl/jupilerproleague/nieuws/article.html?Article_ID=768520|title=KV Mechelen - Club Brugge openingsmatch Jupiler Pro League 2016-2017|work=[[Belgian First Division A]]|date=8 June 2016|access-date=8 June 2016|archive-date=2 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200502063530/https://web.archive.org/web/20171002165658/http://www.sport.be/nl/jupilerproleague/nieuws/article.html?Article_ID=768520|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] were the defending champions but had to settle for second place with [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]] taking their 34th title.

==Team changes==

* [[Oud-Heverlee Leuven|OH Leuven]] was relegated after finishing last in the [[2015–16 Belgian Pro League]].
* Due to the fact that [[2015–16 Belgian Second Division]] champions [[R. White Star Bruxelles|WS Brussels]] were refused a Belgian professional football license, [[K.A.S. Eupen|Eupen]] was promoted as runner-up instead.

==Championship play-offs==
The points obtained during the regular season were halved (and rounded up) before the start of the playoff. As a result, the teams started with the following points before the playoff: Anderlecht 31 points, Club Brugge 30, Zulte Waregem 27, Gent 25, Oostende 25 and Charleroi 25. The points of Anderlecht, Club Brugge and Charleroi were rounded up, therefore in case of any ties on points at the end of the playoffs, the half point would have been deducted for these teams.

==Europa League play-offs==
Group A of the play-offs consisted of the teams finishing in positions 7, 9, 12 and 14 during the [[#Regular season|regular season]] and the first and third placed team in the qualifying positions in the [[2016–17 Belgian First Division B#Aggregate table|2016–17 Belgian First Division B]]. The teams finishing in positions 8, 10, 11, 13 and 15 joined the second placed qualifier from the 2016–17 Belgian First Division B to form group B.

===Semi-final===
The winners of both play-off groups competed in one match to play the fourth-placed or fifth-placed team of the championship play-offs for a spot in the final. This match was played on the field of the highest ranked team in the regular competition. The winner of the semi-final advanced to the final to play for a spot in the [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League#Third qualifying round|third qualifying round]] of the 2017–18 UEFA Europa League.
{{football box
|date       = {{Start date|2017|5|27|df=y}}
|time       = 20:30 [[Central European Summer Time|CEST]]
|team1      = [[K.R.C. Genk|Genk]]
|score      = 3–0
|report     = [http://www.sport.be/nl/jupilerproleague/nieuws/article.html?Article_ID=804821 Pro League]<br/>[https://www.soccerway.com/match/genk-r3jWUIiN/st-truiden-d2EjBxMM/?mid=jJp5Za1p Soccerway]
|team2      = [[Sint-Truidense V.V.|Sint-Truiden]]
|goals1     = [[Thomas Buffel|Buffel]] {{goal|32}}<br/>[[Jean-Paul Boëtius|Boëtius]] {{goal|43}}<br/>[[Mbwana Samatta|Samatta]] {{goal|55}}

===Final===
The winner of the Europa League play-off semi-final and the fourth-placed team played one match to determine the Europa League play-off winner. KV Oostende qualified for the [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League#Third qualifying round|third qualifying round]] of the 2017–18 UEFA Europa League, where they were eliminated by Olympique Marseille.
